title: Analysis: Which countries have sent the most delegates to COP31? - Carbon Brief
gist: Carbon Brief's analysis of UNFCCC provisional lists shows 92,934 in-person registrants for COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, provisionally the largest COP ever, inflated by over 14,000 'host country guests' (vs ~1,000 at COP30). The US under Trump again sent no delegation; Turkey, Brazil, Nigeria, China and Indonesia field the largest delegations.

insights.claim: COP31 in Antalya, Turkey has 92,934 in-person registered participants on UNFCCC provisional lists, provisionally topping COP28 in Dubai (80,000+) as the largest COP in history; including 3,335 virtual delegates the total surpasses 95,000.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Scale of COP attendance signals the summit's continued role as a dealmaking and lobbying venue for energy and climate-exposed sectors.

insights.claim: More than 14,000 COP31 delegates are registered as 'host country guests', versus only about 1,000 in that category on the COP30 Belém provisional list, a large share of COP31's record headcount.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Headline attendance records are partly host-driven; discount crowd size as a gauge of global climate ambition.
insights.locator: Carbon Brief analysis of the provisional lists

insights.claim: COP31's provisional breakdown is parties 18,812, observers 0, media 3,645, overflow 16,726, other/staff 39,400 and virtual 3,335; final UNFCCC figures, based on badges collected at the venue, come only after the summit.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Provisional numbers can be revised down when physical badge pickup is counted.

insights.claim: Party delegates at COP31 total 18,812, the second largest after COP28, and rise to over 34,000 when party-nominated overflow badges are included.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Government negotiating presence remains near record levels despite US absence.

insights.claim: Donald Trump's US government has sent no delegation to COP31, repeating its absence from COP30; Israel and Myanmar are also no-shows.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Continued US federal disengagement from UNFCCC talks leaves China and others to shape outcomes; US policy risk for clean-energy firms persists.
insights.locator: As with COP30, Donald Trump's US government

insights.claim: Despite reports that Taliban officials from Afghanistan had registered as observers for COP31, the provisional lists contain no delegates from observer states.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Minor diplomatic signal; watch for final lists.
insights.locator: It was reported ahead of the summit

insights.claim: Host Turkey registered the largest COP31 delegation (2,950), followed by Brazil (1,994), Nigeria (1,506), China (1,021) and Indonesia (978); Australia, Uganda, Italy, Japan and Kazakhstan round out the top 10, while the UK sent just 255.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Large delegations from Brazil, Nigeria and Indonesia point to emerging-market and forest/fossil-producer interests driving the agenda.

insights.claim: Delegation sizes can be artificially inflated because some countries, such as Brazil, allocate party badges to NGOs.
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Treat delegation size as an imperfect proxy for a government's negotiating weight.

insights.claim: The smallest COP31 delegations come from North Korea (two), Eritrea and Nicaragua (three each), and San Marino and Trinidad and Tobago (four each).
insights.speaker: Carbon Brief Staff
insights.so_what: Low relevance; completeness of the attendance picture.
insights.locator: The smallest delegation comes from North Korea
